paper.title_en: A Scalable 64-Channel Ultra-Stable Bipolar Current Supply for Precision Magnetic Field Control
paper.abstract_en: This paper presents the design, implementation, and experimental validation of a scalable 64-channel ultra-stable bipolar current supply for precision magnetic field control, developed for the TUCAN neutron electric dipole moment (nEDM) experiment. The system employs four 16-channel LTC2668 digital-to-analog converters and precision analog feedback circuitry to deliver independently programmable currents of up to ±40 mA per channel. The architecture emphasizes long-term stability, channel-to-channel consistency, and scalability for large coil arrays. Experimental validation includes long-term stability measurements and a scale-model coil experiment, demonstrating excellent agreement between measured and simulated magnetic fields. The measured current stability exceeds experimental requirements by more than an order of magnitude. The proposed system provides a robust instrumentation platform for high-channel-count precision magnetic field control and is applicable to a broad class of scientific and industrial systems requiring ultra-stable multi-channel current sources.
